contentSections.title: Pre-eclampsia
contentSections.content:
Pre-eclampsia is a serious complication that can seriously affect mum's health and the baby's growth, if not treated early.

This condition develops due to high blood pressure, where blood vessels narrow and limits the blood flow through to vital organs (e.g. brain, kidneys, and liver). One indication of pre-eclampsia is an abnormally high level of protein in the mother's urine, which may suggest compromised kidney function.

Pre-eclampsia can lead to the swelling of mum's hands, feet, and face, as well as dizziness, headaches and an increased risk of stroke and cardiovascular diseases later in life. The reduced blood flow may slow down the growth of the baby, and increases the risk of premature birth (<37 weeks) or stillbirth.

Pre-eclampsia can be detected and managed through regular, careful checks of mum's blood pressure, blood, urine and baby health throughout the pregnancy. Medication and rest is important for keeping the condition under control.
